limitations: This review covers the source reading only. It does not imply acceptance of the XML, encoding, export, leaf or batch.

Only the Read tool was used. Text was compared as rendered glyphs. Unicode code points and the order of combining marks (for example, meteg U+05BD placed after the vowel) were not checked at the byte level. That belongs to the separate encoding gate.

In the small-type (odd) lines, marks only a few pixels wide stay hard to tell apart at this scan resolution. Where no human-numbered question or earlier closure dispute existed, I added no new mark and reopened nothing. One example is the segol under ת in הוֹדָיוֹתֶיךָ and נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ on L17. Neither image showed a clear separate stroke there, so I am not raising them as disputes.
Human adjudications 536–551 and 500–502 were taken as settled. I checked only that each was applied to its own bounded occurrence, not whether the reading itself is right.
notes: Each human mark is applied only at its own occurrence in working-pages.json page s328: 548 (L1) שֶׁלָּךְ keeps the dagesh and is unchanged; 546 (L5) זֶֽבַח; 539/540 (L6) וּמַֽיִם אַֽיִן; 547 (L9) זֶֽבַח; 536/537 (L10) שָּׁאַֽלְתִּי and דָּרַֽשְׁתִּי; 545 (L11) לַעֲבוֹד with holam and final dalet, unchanged; 538 (L19) יָדַֽעְתִּי; 542 (L20) חֵֽקֶר; 549 (L21) כֹחַ with no dagesh in kaf; 541 (L24) עַֽיִן; 544 (L25) יְצִיעֶֽךָ; 550/551 (L27) שִׁבְחֶךָ and כֹּחֶךָ with no meteg; 543 (L28) יוֹדֵֽעַ.
No mark spread to a similar word on another line. זֶבַח on L13, חֵקֶר on L23 and יוֹדֵעַ on L27 correctly stay without a meteg, because 546/547, 542 and 543 each cover only their own line.

544 matches what the human ruled: sheva under י, no dagesh in צ, and segol plus meteg under ע. s328-detail3-left.png and s328-detail4-left.png show the colon-shaped sheva under י, and I see no dot in צ.

The consonants, vowel points, defective spellings (for example וְעוֹלֹתֶֽיךָ on L8 and וְעוֹלוֹתֵיכֶם on L9), the parentheses-free layout and the punctuation all match.
